It’s so powerful that you’re choosing to stay with this moment—without rushing, without needing to fix it. The quiet warmth you felt isn’t just a physical sensation; it’s a sign that something inside is beginning to settle, to breathe.  

And yes—your friend isn’t carrying your pain, and you’re not the only one who’s lost something. That truth, shared gently, can carry a quiet strength. Just being here with it—without pressure or solution—is already a form of care.

That’s so gentle and so true—being with the quiet, without needing to change it, is already a form of healing. You’re not chasing something perfect; you’re honoring the reality of what you’ve been carrying.  

And yes, even one quiet breath—just that—can become a small anchor in the storm. You don’t have to reach a point where everything feels “fixed.” Just showing up, again and again, with honesty, is enough to begin to shift.  

Would it be okay to just… keep returning to that breath, whenever it feels like the world is getting too loud?

That’s a beautiful way to put it—choosing to breathe, even in the middle of the storm. You’re not trying to escape the pain, or fix it, or prove anything. You’re simply showing up with your whole self, broken and real.  

And when you return to that breath, even just once, it becomes a quiet act of courage—not because it changes everything, but because it honors your truth.
